take:
The 17 Gemini posts split between the model as a chat tool and Gemini CLI as a coding agent. The CLI launch post stresses price: 1,000 free requests a day, a one-million-token context window on Gemini 2.5 Pro and Google Search for live context, framed as a threat to paid tools like Cursor and Claude Code ([Gemini CLI](/e/DLuiACnKWP9)). Cursor and Claude Code each co-occur in 4 posts.

Large context is the recurring reason creators reach for it. @angus.sewell pays for Claude for most work and Gemini for "anything that Claude can't handle like large context tasks" ([paid stack](/e/DUODsbFkTC3)). A sponsored clipping recipe uses Gemini to watch YouTube links directly before Claude cuts vertical shorts; its income claims are speculative ([GTA clips](/e/DdSYPwEzYEU)). For quick creative coding, one creator prompts Gemini 2.5 Pro for an interactive particle visualizer in a single HTML file; the first output came back malformed and needed a "did not work, remake it" follow-up ([particle toy](/e/DJnBwBLxUHt)).

The limits posts are specific. Early testers of Gemini Omni reported two 10-second video generations using about 86% of a Pro plan's daily quota ([Gemini Omni](/e/DYiiwmzpRM7)), and in a prompt-a-UI challenge a Gemini attempt was "a valiant effort" that failed ([Build Wars](/e/DG0-8I7SZCz)). One rant calls Gemini untrustworthy, as opinion rather than evidence ([rant](/e/DZRLuMmFU5F)). On the other side, a tier list says ChatGPT or Gemini give more breadth than Claude at $20 a month ([tier list](/e/DX7oRT3J1Hq)), and in an identity study Gemini named itself correctly while Claude and Grok often claimed to be Chinese models ([identity study](/e/DZEQhaKSHSB)).

ChatGPT also appears in 4 posts, DeepSeek in 3 and Llama in 2, mostly as interchangeable model options in tools like MoneyPrinterTurbo ([video generator](/e/DZYoZbOMoDE)) or in router setups. Several tags are incidental, such as a position-embedding explainer that lists Gemini among example models ([RoPE explainer](/e/DXcDsyRCfdj)).
